item.content:encoded: Meh. Decent concept but very boring and barebones execution. I'm all for cool ideas that aren't bogged down with extraneous test logs and interviews (like SCP-1489 or SCP-1959, but for those types of skips the core idea has to be interesting enough to merit being on its own. In this case, the concept failed to retain my interest due to how plainly it was executed and presented. Downvoting.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Damn, this thread is ancient. If anyone still cares, I'd suggest detailing tests that delved into the physical means by which the two are able to share stimuli across a physical divide, if any. The entry hints at 'lag' when the two are far apart, which suggests that there is something at work like a signal that is constrained by such things as distance, speed of transmission, and possibly even signal integrity. There's definitely potential for an interesting experiment log if a section along these lines is added and well executed.

And if an individual opinion isn't quite convincing enough, it's certainly seems like something The Foundation would have thought to test. Extensively so, even, perhaps attempting to replicate the means of 'telepathy' once it is pinned down…and/or using electromagnets/lead barriers/tin foil hats to try to disrupt the connection.

All that rambling aside, it's a decent entry. My vote is currently neutral because of the unused potential I see here.
